title: Documenting the incident: symptom, hypothesis, test and fix

videos.script: Lesson 21 found a fault that let small things through a tunnel and swallowed large ones. {{case}} It took a handful of commands to find, and two rules on one router to fix. Now imagine it comes back in a year, on another tunnel, with somebody else on call. {{again}} If nothing was written down, they start from zero. If the last person wrote four things down, they start from the answer. What went wrong. What was suspected. How each suspicion was tested. And what fixed it. {{record}} This lesson is about writing that record. When to note the time, and in which time zone, so that two logs can be lined up. {{time}} How to write about a mistake without writing about a person, because the rule behind this fault looks like one written to make a router safer. {{blameless}} And what an action item needs before anybody will do it: an owner, and a way to tell that it is done. {{actions}} The lab has no incident of its own for this lesson. It writes up the one from lesson 21, using only what that lesson's transcripts printed. {{writeup}}
